item.title: Oze National Park: Skunk Cabbage & High-Altitude Wetlands from Gunma — Guide
item.description: Oze National Park, a vast high-altitude wetland straddling Gunma, Fukushima, Niigata and Tochigi prefectures, is accessible from Gunma’s Hinoemata trailheads and protected as a national park since 2007. Wooden boardwalks wind through the fragile marsh ecosystem, famous each June for spectacular blooms of white skunk cabbage (mizubasho) carpeting the wetland, followed by alpine wildflowers through summer, with Mt. Shibutsu rising above the plain and offering more demanding hiking for those wanting mountain views.

item.title: Oze Marshland National Park: Japan's High-Altitude Wetland — Guide
item.description: Oze Marshland National Park is one of Japan’s great wilderness areas, a vast high-altitude wetland straddling Fukushima, Gunma, Niigata and Tochigi prefectures, protected as a national park since 2007. Wooden boardwalks wind through the marsh, letting hikers explore without disturbing the fragile peat-bog ecosystem, famous each May and June for spectacular blooms of white skunk cabbage (mizubasho) followed by alpine wildflowers through summer, with Mt. Shibutsu rising above the plain.

item.title: Gunma Nature: Oze National Park, Mt. Akagi & Lake Haruna
item.description: Gunma’s mountains cover the greater part of the prefecture, rising from the flat Kanto plain in the south to volcanic ridges and alpine wetlands along the northern border with Niigata and Fukushima. The variety of terrain is wide — ancient shield volcanoes with caldera lakes, narrow river gorges cut by glacial meltwater, and elevated marshes that exist only because the altitude keeps them frozen for half the year. For outdoor travelers, Gunma is one of the most rewarding prefectures within two hours of Tokyo.
